newsitem.title: GREECE: ZENECA NO COMMENT ON GREEK TOMATO REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ZENECA NO COMMENT ON GREEK TOMATO REPORT.

text.p: Zeneca Group Plc on Wednesday declined to comment on reports Greece may decide to scrap gene-tomato research carried out by the British drugs and agrochemicals company.
"We have had no direct communication with the Greek government and therefore we cannot comment at the moment," a Zeneca spokeswoman said.
She was speaking after Greenpeace activists on Tuesday said the Greek government would consider withdrawing a permit granting Zeneca to conduct field trials with genetically altered tomatoes.
Zeneca conducts similar trails in Britain, France, Italy, Spain and Portugal and is currently seeking European Union approval to grow and sell the new tomatoes across Europe.
The genetically-modified fruit is already grown in the U.S. and allowed to be marketed as puree in Britain. It is sold here by supermarket chains for over a year without any marked opposition.
The new tomatoes have an extended ripening time, which means puree makers need less heat to process the fruit.
Greenpeace and other environmental groups have launched an international campaign against gene-altered foods, saying there may be unknown health risks.
